clue.text: Thus illuminated by a flickering ray alone

parts.note: thus means so, as in 'so be it'
illuminated means lit

indicators.note: a flickering light wavers about, so the letters of ray are jumbled

explanation.surface: A lone figure is lit by the wavering beam of a single light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flickering' rearranges RAY to ARY; 'by a' just joins SO and LIT to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone solitary is by themselves, without company.

clue.text: A foot of water to decide about

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: to see is to decide, as in 'I'll see what to do'
a pond is a body of water

explanation.surface: Someone must make a call concerning twelve inches of water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foot' is metrical: a spondee is two stressed syllables.
explanation.definitionFit: A spondee is a metrical unit of two long or stressed syllables in verse.

clue.text: Pay attention to one curious nest in the heather

indicators.note: in puts these inside the heather

parts.note: ling is a common name for heather
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: curious means odd, so the letters of nest are arranged oddly

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher is urged to observe an odd nest among moorland plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curious' gives STEN; 'heather' is the plant's other name, common in British moorland, which 'in' opens up.
explanation.definitionFit: Listening means attending closely to sounds or speech; the participle stands in for the instruction loosely.

clue.text: Tin fish roped to wreck

indicators.note: to wreck the words before it is to smash their letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Lashing things together could sink a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is ROPED plus TO, shuffled; 'Tin fish' is old naval slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Tin fish was naval slang for a self-propelled underwater missile.

clue.text: McAdam, for example, introducing notice in upright type

indicators.note: introducing means the notice is put inside the type

parts.note: roman is the upright typeface, as opposed to italic
an ad is a notice in a paper

explanation.surface: A Scottish engineer's name appears in an announcement set in plain upright print.
explanation.walkthrough: John McAdam was a road builder who gave us macadam surfacing.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadman is a road builder or mender, which John McAdam was.

clue.text: Great lady's illegal marriage

parts.note: great means big
Amy stands for a lady here, a girl's name taken as any woman

explanation.surface: A grand dame has entered into a marriage the law forbids.
explanation.definitionFit: Bigamy is the crime of marrying while already married to someone else.

clue.text: Money policy on which one is penurious

parts.note: bread is slang for money
a line is a policy, as in the party line

explanation.surface: A government's financial strategy leaves people poor.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on the breadline is to be very poor, with barely enough to live on.

clue.text: The colour of grouse, for example, coming out of a swamp

indicators.note: coming out of means the bird spreads out around the swamp, on either side

parts.note: grouse is an example of game birds
a bog is a swamp

explanation.surface: A game bird emerging from marshland shows a particular shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming out of' is unusual: the bird emerges on both sides of the swamp, so the container wraps round it rather than sitting inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Gamboge is a deep yellow pigment from a tree resin, and the shade named after it.

clue.text: Virtuoso in West Street rules out introductions

parts.note: Mae West was the American film star

indicators.note: introductions are the opening letters of the words rules and out

explanation.surface: A brilliant performer in a London road says the regulations forbid making acquaintances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West' is not a direction but the actress Mae West; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A maestro is a master performer, especially a great conductor or musician.

clue.text: Can perhaps put in notice for the ceremony

indicators.note: put in tells us one piece is placed within another

parts.note: to notice something is to observe it

indicators.note: perhaps marks the word can as possibly arranged otherwise, a loose sign to shuffle it

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a can might be inserted into an announcement about a ritual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' at the start looks like a verb; 'perhaps' makes it ANC, which 'put in' sets in the notice.
explanation.definitionFit: An observance is a rite or customary ceremonial act.

clue.text: They are blessed with great expectations

definitions.text: They are blessed with great expectations

parts.words: They are blessed with great expectations
parts.note: the Beatitudes promise that the humble will inherit the earth: blessed indeed, with a vast legacy to come

explanation.walkthrough: The Dickens novel title is a decoy; the expectations are the inheritance of the earth in the Sermon on the Mount.
explanation.definitionFit: Matthew 5:5 calls the humble and gentle blessed, for they shall inherit the earth.

clue.text: Something said in ""The Queen's Arms"

parts.note: the clue reads like a remark overheard in a pub, but it means the motto written on the British sovereign's coat of arms

explanation.walkthrough: The Queen's Arms sounds like a pub name; the arms are the royal coat of arms, whose motto, French for 'God and my right', appears on it.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase is the motto of the British monarch, inscribed on the royal coat of arms.

clue.text: Parasite found in animal enclosure in Broken Pine

indicators.note: in puts the enclosure inside the broken word
broken means the letters of pine are smashed and reassembled

parts.note: a zoo is a place where animals are kept enclosed

explanation.surface: A bug turns up in a pen of creatures kept among some damaged pine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broken' gives EPIN, and 'in' opens it; 'found' only joins definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An epizoon is a creature living on the outside of another animal, feeding off it.

clue.text: Display too much on deck

parts.note: over can mean on, as in a cover over or on a bed
to deck is to dress or adorn

explanation.surface: Showing off too much while standing on the ship's deck.
explanation.definitionFit: To overdress is to dress or adorn too elaborately, making too much show.

clue.text: Sack despicable fellow for support of conflagration

parts.note: to sack someone is to fire them
a dog is slang for a contemptible man

explanation.surface: A rotten worker is dismissed for propping up a blaze.
explanation.definitionFit: A firedog, or andiron, is a metal stand holding logs in a fireplace.

clue.text: In conversation, splendid celebrity makes a bloomer

indicators.note: in conversation means the words are heard spoken, giving a word that sounds alike

parts.note: dandy means splendid, and a lion is a celebrity, as in a literary lion

explanation.surface: Chatting, a fine famous person makes a gaffe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a blunder, but here it is a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is anything that flowers, and this yellow-flowered weed is one.

clue.text: Beneficiary of an opening in the shelter

indicators.note: in places the opening inside the shelter

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind
a gate is an opening in a wall or fence

explanation.surface: Someone benefits from a gap in a protective covering.
explanation.definitionFit: A legatee is the person who receives a bequest under a will.

clue.text: European cardinal points outside to master

indicators.note: outside means the points surround the European

parts.note: ENE, east-north-east, is a compass point built from cardinal points
a Slav is a European of Slavic stock

explanation.surface: A churchman from the continent points outside, to take control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European' looks like E, but it is SLAV; 'cardinal' is not a churchman; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To enslave someone is to subjugate them, becoming their master.

clue.text: A winning way in opposition

parts.note: gain means winning, a profit
St is street, a way

explanation.surface: A victorious route is resisted.
explanation.definitionFit: Against means opposed to or contrary to something.

clue.text: Put money into old coin — it's like a bit of hindsight

indicators.note: into puts the money inside the coin

parts.note: the real was an old Spanish silver coin
tin is old slang for money

explanation.surface: Investing in an antique coin is wise only in retrospect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hindsight' is split: the retina sits at the back of the eye, a bit of sight at the hind end.
explanation.definitionFit: Retinal means relating to the retina, the light-sensitive layer at the back of the eyeball.

clue.text: Soldier is bound by religious rule

definitions.meaning: a professional soldier in a standing army
... clergy are those living under a monastic rule

explanation.definitionFit: Regular means both a full-time professional soldier and clergy living under a monastic order's rule.

clue.text: Nothing is raised in rent by twisting

indicators.note: in puts the reversed pieces inside the rent

parts.note: rent means torn

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means read upwards, so the pieces are reversed

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A tearing landlord says no one gets a rise in rent by twisting things.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'raised' reads upwards, giving SIO; 'in' sets it in the rent, and 'by' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Torsion is the action of twisting something about an axis.

clue.text: Angela's exotic food

indicators.note: exotic means foreign and strange, so the letters are made strange

parts.note: taken as written, with the possessive s counted

explanation.surface: A woman named Angela cooks something foreign.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the 's is a letter of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasagne is an Italian pasta dish of baked layered sheets.

clue.text: Army regulations such as "Attention" and "At ease'?

definitions.meaning: permanent rules governing a military unit's conduct
these are commands given to soldiers who are on their feet in formation

explanation.definitionFit: Standing orders are fixed rules, and also, playfully, commands given to troops who are upright on parade.

clue.text: Girl said to be a religious type here

indicators.note: said means the girl's name is heard, giving a word spoken alike

parts.note: Jane is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman is reported to be the pious sort around these parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jain follows Jainism, an Indian religion stressing non-violence.

clue.text: Crying out about former spouse making demands

parts.note: an ex is a former husband or wife
claiming means demanding as one's right

explanation.surface: Someone protests loudly about a past partner who keeps asking for things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is a link here, not the C for circa.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclaim is to shout out suddenly, so exclaiming means shouting aloud in surprise.

clue.text: Matches an article in clothing

indicators.note: in puts the article inside the clothing

parts.note: vests are items of clothing
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A box of lights is tucked inside an item of underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Vestas were a type of short wax friction match.

clue.text: Soldiers — Lancers, perhaps receiving new guns

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

indicators.note: receiving means the dance takes the letter inside it

parts.note: the Lancers is a quadrille, an example of a dance

explanation.surface: A cavalry regiment is being issued fresh weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lancers are not cavalry here but a 19th-century square dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordnance means artillery, mounted guns and their supplies.
